message.content:
json
{
  "verdict": "request",
  "cause": "IMAGE_FIELD_IGNORED",
  "fix": {"action": "change_request_format", "target": "messages[].content", "value": "send content as an array of parts: [{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"...\"},{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":{\"url\":\"data:image/png;base64,<b64>\"}}] and drop the custom \"images\" key"},
  "rationale": "The base64 PNG is placed in a custom \"images\" field with content as a plain string, which is the Ollama-style shape; llama-server's OpenAI-compatible endpoint only reads images from content parts of type image_url containing a data URI, so the image is silently ignored. The usage stats confirm this: prompt_tokens is only 21, far too few for an encoded image, which would contribute hundreds of tokens via the projector. The projector itself is loaded (--mmproj is in the launch command), so the runtime is fine and the model truthfully reports it received no picture."
}
